note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published on PlayStation (via Exophase and PSNProfiles). Every guide below is written in our own words for this journal; sources are cited per trophy and were never copied.
title: Leonida Field Journal — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy data

trophies.guide: The platinum lands on its own once the other 54 are done — there is no separate task behind it. Treat it as the journal's last page: finish the story, clear the 100% checklist, then sweep the stragglers. PowerPyx puts the whole run at roughly 200 hours, difficulty 4/10.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order.
Check the Up Next planner when you stall — it always points at the cheapest remaining trophy.
Do not use cheats: they disable trophies and saving.

trophies.guide: Story trophy — it pops when the opening mission Gone Fishing is done, so you cannot miss it by playing normally. It is hidden on PSN until earned, which is why the spoiler toggle keeps it veiled in this journal. Just play the opening and it is yours.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Play the opening mission Gone Fishing to its end.
No side task is needed; the trophy follows the story.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 1. Before you leave the chapter, do the one thing this journal warns about everywhere: meditate with Lucia on the balcony at Jason's house after the mission Down to Earth — that first meditation spot is the only one reported missable in the whole game.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Finish every mission in Chapter 1.
Before the chapter ends, take Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house (see Positive Mental Attitude).

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 2 — it arrives with the chapter's last mission and needs no extra work. The name is printed on PSN with asterisks, exactly as shown here. Keep playing the story and it pops on its own.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Play through Chapter 2 to its final mission.
No collectible or side task is attached to it.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 3. By now the map is wide open, so use the travel between missions to scan vehicles and study animals through the binoculars — that slow background progress pays off later on the 100% checklist.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Finish Chapter 3's missions in order.
Between missions, scan new vehicles and study animals when you spot them.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 4 — the last chapter before the finale. If any stranger or side-mission strand is still open, clear what you can before the final mission, while the world is still calm and every contact is reachable.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Finish Chapter 4.
Sweep up any open stranger strands before starting the finale.

trophies.guide: Gold story trophy for the final mission — the credits roll and free-roam opens up afterwards, so nothing in the story is left behind. The 100% Completion checklist appears under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion once the story is done, and earlier progress already counts toward it.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Complete the final mission.
After the credits, open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion to see what is left.

trophies.guide: Story trophy tied to the mission Breakfast Run. It unlocks as part of the main story, so there is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — just keep following the mission thread when it appears.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Play the mission Breakfast Run when the story offers it.
Finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for The Cartel Heist mission. Heist missions in this game are story beats, not the repeatable bank jobs of free-roam — finish this one when it comes up and the trophy follows. The repeatable vault robberies belong to Maximum Withdrawal instead.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Play The Cartel Heist when the story reaches it.
Finish the mission to pop the trophy.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Child's Play. Like the other mission trophies it is unmissable — the story hands it to you. Keep an eye on the mission's own objectives on screen; there is no hidden requirement behind the name.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Play Child's Play when the story offers it.
Complete its objectives; the trophy pops at the end.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Headliners. It pops at the mission's end with no extra condition, so play it like any other story mission. The all-caps title is PSN's own spelling, kept exactly as published.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Play Headliners when the story reaches it.
Finish the mission.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the VCIA Takedown mission. VCIA — the Vice City airport — also shows up in the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can, but this one is purely a story beat: finish the takedown and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Play VCIA Takedown when the story offers it.
Complete the mission.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for Operation Savage Glory, the last of the named mission trophies. It is unmissable and story-only — finish the operation and it pops. With the mission trophies done, the story set is complete except the chapter and finale trophies.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Play Operation Savage Glory when the story reaches it.
Finish the mission.

trophies.guide: The hardest trophy in the set, and the gold that gates the platinum. The checklist unlocks after the story under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion — and it is kinder than it sounds: PowerPyx calls it closer to 60% true completion, needing 200 of 277 vehicles, 100 of 255 animals, 50 of 66 weapons and 70 of 80 challenges, so you can skip the hardest challenges. Only robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests need everything.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish the story to unlock the 100% checklist.
Work the checklist in the journal's Stage 6 order: robberies, ranges, races, then leftovers.
You only need 70 of 80 challenges — skip the ones that fight you.

trophies.guide: Silver for 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime and the like, counted across the whole game. There are 397 stunts in Leonida and the 100% checklist wants 300, so the trophy's 250 comes first and the extra 50 fold into A Long Road. Chain them during normal driving and the count climbs without a dedicated grind.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Play normally and take jumps and ramps when you see them — stunts count anywhere.
Hunt the marked stunt jumps when the counter stalls.
250 of 397 is enough; the last 50 toward 300 belong to the 100% checklist.

trophies.desc: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Bronze for sampling all 9 activity types once — you only have to try each, not win or master it. This is the game's taster trophy: dip into fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling and the rest, and it pops when the ninth type is touched. A good first-hour trophy if you like ticking boxes early.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Open the activities list and try one of each of the 9 types.
Losing counts — you only need to take part once per type.

trophies.desc: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver for gold-medalling all 42 Shooting Range challenges. The ranges are repeatable, so a failed run costs nothing but time — learn each range's target pattern, then go for gold one range at a time. All 42 golds are also required for the 100% checklist, so this trophy does double duty.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Visit every shooting range and learn its challenge.
Replay each until you hold gold on all 42.
Use Combat Focus habits from the story — steady aim beats fast fire.

trophies.desc: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Bronze for winning a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location is its own race, so this is a tour of Leonida by drone — win one race per spot and the trophy pops. Drone races also feed the 100% checklist, so the wins count twice.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find each of the 14 Top Fun drone race locations.
Win at least one race at every location.
Replay a location if you lose — the win is what counts.

trophies.guide: Bronze for winning 20 different races — different events, not the same race twenty times. Mix vehicle races and drone races across the map; every fresh event you win ticks the counter. If a race keeps beating you, switch to an easier event and come back later with a better vehicle.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Enter races across Leonida — land, water and drone events all count.
Win 20 distinct events; repeats of one event do not add up.
Upgrade or swap vehicles for the races that resist you.

trophies.desc: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Bronze for beating Cal in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head fishing contest, not just catching a fish. Learn the fishing rhythm first on your own (cast, wait for the bite, reel steady), then take Cal on when your timing feels reliable. Losing costs nothing; challenge him again.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Practice fishing until the bite-and-reel rhythm feels natural.
Take Cal's fishing challenge and out-fish him.
Retry as often as needed — the challenge stays open.

trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing a single arcade game — the quickest activity trophy in the journal. Walk into an arcade, pick any cabinet, and play it through to the end. It also ticks one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so do it early.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade and pick any game cabinet.
Play it through to completion — one finished game is enough.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing Andy's mission strand — play his missions in order until the final one. Side strands like Andy's unlock as the story progresses, so if his marker is not on the map yet, keep playing the story and check back. The final mission is the one that pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Follow Andy's missions as they appear.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing Kenton's mission strand. Kenton's jobs involve boats — keep a fast boat in mind when his missions start stacking up. Play his strand to its final mission and the trophy pops; like the other side strands, it is not missable once unlocked.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Play Kenton's missions in order as they appear.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing Billy's mission strand. Billy's missions are built around riding, so a good bike helps the chases go smoothly. Follow the strand to its final mission — the trophy pops there, not at the first job.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Play Billy's missions in order as they appear.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.desc: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver for completing 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida — the game's oddballs, each with their own little chain of jobs. The named side strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret) feed this count, so finishing them already does most of the work; pick up the remaining stranger markers on the map to reach 8.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Finish the named side strands — each one counts.
Take stranger markers you pass on the map until 8 strands are complete.
Strands unlock with story progress; revisit the map after each chapter.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing Randy's mission strand. Randy's jobs revolve around supply runs — expect driving and delivery under pressure rather than straight shootouts. Play the strand through to its final mission.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Play Randy's missions in order as they appear.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing Tyrone's mission strand. Tyrone's jobs are DJ-flavoured — the strand is short and the final mission is the one that matters. If his marker is missing, push the story forward; side strands open up as chapters pass.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Play Tyrone's missions in order as they appear.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.desc: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: The only missable trophy in the game — and the one this whole journal is built around. There are 18 meditation spots in 10 locations, and the FIRST one can be lost: after the mission Down to Earth in Chapter 1, Lucia invites Jason to meditate on the balcony at his house in the morning. Take it before Chapter 1 ends or it is gone for the playthrough. The other 17 spots stay available in free-roam.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Chapter 1, after Down to Earth: find Lucia at Jason's house in the morning and accept the balcony meditation — do this before the chapter ends.
Afterwards, meditate at the remaining 17 spots across Leonida (10 locations in total).
If the first spot is gone, only a new playthrough can save the trophy — so do it first.

trophies.desc: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bronze for hunting a unique animal for Bret — his strand is the game's hunting questline, and this trophy is its trophy. Study animals through the binoculars on the way: the 100% checklist wants 100 of 255 animals studied, so every animal you scope now counts twice. Bret's quests also need full completion for the 100% checklist.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Start Bret's strand and follow his hunting jobs.
Hunt the unique animal he asks for.
Scope animals with binoculars along the way — it feeds the 100% checklist.

trophies.guide: Silver for completing 3 collectible card sets. There are 18 sets scattered across Leonida and the 100% checklist wants 15 of them, so this trophy's 3 sets are just the opening hand — collect every card you pass and the sets complete themselves. Cards hide in shops, homes and odd corners, so check interiors as you travel.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Pick up every collectible card you find while travelling.
Complete any 3 full sets — the trophy pops at the third.
Keep collecting: 15 sets feed the 100% checklist.

trophies.guide: Silver for using WAiNK It at 100 locations — the game's photo-tagging collectible, done at landmarks and viewpoints across the state. All 100 locations are also required for the 100% checklist, so none of this work is wasted. Tag a spot whenever the prompt appears and the count climbs as you explore.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Use WAiNK It at every landmark or viewpoint the game offers.
Reach 100 tagged locations.
Pair it with exploring: new areas often hold new WAiNK spots.

trophies.guide: Bronze for finishing 50 challenges — the game's scattered mini-objectives, from stunt chains to combat feats. There are 80 in total and the 100% checklist wants 70, so the trophy's 50 is the halfway mark, not the end. Do the easy ones first; the hardest can be skipped entirely for 100%.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the challenges list and clear the easy ones first.
Reach 50 completed challenges.
Keep going toward 70 for the 100% checklist — the hardest 10 can be skipped.

trophies.desc: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Bronze for shaking a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then escaping clean. The trick is the partner: do it during a mission or free-roam stretch where Lucia or Jason is riding along, build the heat to 4 stars, then break line of sight and lay low until the stars clear. A fast car and a quiet corner do the rest.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Play with your partner beside you and build a 4-star wanted level.
Break line of sight and hide until the wanted level clears.
Escape without being spotted again — the trophy pops on the getaway.

trophies.desc: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Bronze for robbing 3 shops back-to-back with your partner while keeping your wanted level the whole way — the catch is you must NOT lose the heat between robberies. Pick three shops close together, plan the route, and hit them fast one after another with your partner along. Losing the wanted level resets the chain, so keep moving.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Rob 3 shops close together.
Rob the first, keep your wanted level, and drive straight to the next.
Rob all 3 without the heat dropping — the trophy pops at the third.

trophies.guide: Bronze for discovering 100 vehicles — getting in and driving a new model counts as a discovery. The 100% checklist wants 200 of 277, so this trophy is the halfway point of a much longer collection. Scan every new vehicle you drive and the count climbs on its own during normal play.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive every new vehicle model you come across.
Reach 100 discovered vehicles.
Keep scanning toward 200 for the 100% checklist.

trophies.desc: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Bronze for dropping 5 enemies inside one use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-mo aiming mode. Set it up where enemies bunch together: trigger Combat Focus with a full group in view, work through them quickly, and do not let the meter run out before the fifth falls. A busy shootout is the best stage for it.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a fight with at least 5 enemies grouped together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down 5 before it ends.
Retry in the next big shootout if the meter runs dry.

trophies.desc: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Bronze for an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the Vice City airport. In plain terms: get a plane off the ground at the airport without going through the normal channels. Grab an aircraft on the tarmac and take off; the trophy pops once you are airborne on your own terms.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Go to VCIA, the Vice City airport.
Get into a plane and take off without a scheduled departure.
The trophy pops once you are airborne.

trophies.guide: Bronze with a joke for a description — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' points at the Rhino tank. The trophy is about tangling with tanks: get into a Rhino, or survive a confrontation with one, and the trophy follows. The exact trigger is tied to the tank itself, so make the Rhino the centre of the attempt.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Find a Rhino tank — military areas are the place to look.
Get into it or take the fight to it.
The trophy pops from the tank encounter.

trophies.desc: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Bronze for robbing a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery, not a smash-and-grab. Case the store first, go in quiet, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again with a cleaner plan.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Rob it without being detected at any point.
If spotted, leave and retry — detection voids the attempt.

trophies.guide: Silver for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping each time. Vault jobs are the heavy end of the robbery list — plan the getaway before the alarm, not after. All vault robberies are also required for the 100% checklist, so these five count twice.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find bank vault robbery opportunities across Leonida.
Rob a vault and escape cleanly — repeat for 5 vaults.
Plan the getaway route before you go in.

trophies.desc: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Bronze for robbing an armored truck and escaping — the classic GTA heist in miniature. Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida; intercept one, stop it, take the cash and lose the heat. One clean job is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on its route.
Stop it, take the cash, and escape.
One successful escape pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Bronze for exploring all 52 areas of Leonida — the whole map, from Vice City to the swamps and keys. The counter ticks as you enter each named area, so a slow road trip that touches every corner does the job. Pair it with the WAiNK spots and card hunting: one trip, three counters.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Travel through every named area of Leonida — 52 in total.
The counter ticks on entry; no task is needed inside each area.
Combine the trip with WAiNK tags and card pickups.

trophies.desc: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Bronze for robbing one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gang operations are marked targets around the map — hit one per gang and the set is complete. These robberies also feed the 100% checklist, which wants every gang operation, so the trophy is the first pass over a longer list.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Find illegal operation targets for each of the 9 gangs.
Rob one operation per gang.
Keep going after the trophy — the 100% checklist wants all of them.

trophies.desc: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Bronze for enjoying a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — one of the game's quiet moment trophies. Head to a bar or spot with a view over Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take it in. It is a breather trophy: slow down, sit, drink, done.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Go to Ocean Beach and find a spot with a view.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.
The trophy pops once the moment registers.

trophies.desc: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Bronze for smashing your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, GTA-style. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or aimed at it, and floor it through the front. The trophy is about the exit, so make it loud.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Drive a vehicle out through the showroom front in classic style.
The trophy pops on the smash exit.

trophies.desc: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bronze for a follow-through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — bowl a game there and finish it. Bowling is one of the 9 activity types, so this also ticks Master of None. It is a nod to the series' past: just play a full game at that specific alley.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play a full game of bowling there.
Finish the game — the trophy pops on the follow-through.

trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — no verified method yet. The description hints at a partnership moment with mass appeal, but no guide has pinned down the exact trigger, and this journal will not guess one. Check the cited sources for the latest player reports before chasing it; if a method appears, it will be the partnership activity the community settles on.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: No verified steps yet — do not trust a method with no source.
Watch the cited guides for player-confirmed reports.
Keep playing story and partner activities; the trigger will surface in the community.

trophies.guide: Bronze tied to the choices you make across the game — PSN tracks a count toward 500. The description is deliberately vague, but the counter is the clue: keep making story and side choices as you play and the count climbs. It is a long-haul trophy that fills itself in during a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Keep playing and making choices in story and side content.
The PSN counter tracks toward 500.
It fills over a full playthrough — no single mission unlocks it.

trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — no verified method yet. 'Second time's the charm' suggests succeeding at something on a second attempt, but no guide has confirmed which event or activity the trophy watches, and this journal will not invent one. Wait for a player-confirmed report in the cited sources before spending time on it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: No verified steps yet — do not trust a method with no source.
Watch the cited guides for player-confirmed reports.
If you fail something and succeed on the retry, note what it was — the community is still mapping this one.

trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — no verified method yet. The description reads like a reaction to something strange — an odd encounter or event somewhere in Leonida — but no guide has confirmed what triggers it, and this journal will not guess. Explore the map's odd corners and watch the cited sources for the first confirmed sighting.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: No verified steps yet — do not trust a method with no source.
Explore Leonida's strange spots and watch the cited guides.
The trigger is likely a one-off world event; the community is still finding it.

trophies.desc: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bronze for bowling someone over with a melee drive-by — strike a pedestrian with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a target, swing the melee weapon from the vehicle, and the knockdown pops the trophy. Pick a quiet street so the wanted level stays manageable.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Get in a vehicle with a melee weapon ready.
Drive past a pedestrian and land a melee hit from the vehicle.
The knockdown pops the trophy — keep the speed low so the swing connects.

trophies.desc: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Bronze for laundering $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists — they are dirty money until a contact cleans them. Keep running jobs, keep laundering the take, and the counter reaches $250,000 over the course of the money grind.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts.
Repeat until $250,000 is laundered.

trophies.guide: Bronze for spending $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, food, anything with a price tag. The money you launder for Dime on the Dollar has to go somewhere, and this is where: buy the gear you actually want and the counter fills itself. Big-ticket vehicles help if the total stalls.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Spend money in any shops — clothes, weapons, food, vehicles.
Reach $100,000 total spent.
Buy big-ticket items if the counter stalls near the end.

trophies.guide: Bronze for buying all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought with clean money, so this trophy sits at the end of the money chain: rob, launder, then spend on property. Each garage also stores your growing vehicle collection for Whip It Good, so the purchase pays twice.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Earn and launder money through robberies and contacts.
Buy each of the 8 garage properties.
The trophy pops at the eighth purchase.

trophies.desc: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Bronze for registering 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game delivery-style app for two-wheelers and small vehicles. Find ten different vehicles, register each through the app, and the trophy pops. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you discover is a registration candidate.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app in-game.
Register 10 different vehicles through it.
Use newly discovered vehicles — they count for Whip It Good too.
